title: Game Theory (HL) Adventure 3: Sequential Games
welcome_lead: Today you'll solve sequential games with backward induction.
meta_desc: Economics HL Game Theory: simultaneous vs sequential games, game trees, backward induction.
final_note: You distinguished simultaneous from sequential games and used backward induction.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Simultaneous (normal form): a matrix; no player observes the other.

Sequential (extensive form): a game tree; later movers see earlier moves.

Sequential games suit entry decisions, leader/follower price-setting (Stackelberg), bargaining.

Solve from the last move backwards.

Example: incumbent vs entrant. Entrant 'Enter' or 'Stay'. If Enter, incumbent 'Fight' or 'Accommodate'.

Payoffs: (Stay,.)=(0,5); (Enter, Fight)=(−3,0); (Enter, Accommodate)=(2,2).

Incumbent will choose Accommodate (2 > 0); knowing that, the entrant enters. SPNE: (Enter, Accommodate).

Threats only deter if they are credible.

'Fight' here is not credible — once entry occurs it's worse for the incumbent. Commitment devices (excess capacity, contracts) can make threats credible and shape outcomes — Stackelberg leadership.

mcqs.q: Are monopolies always bad for consumers?
options: A monopoly is when one country dominates world trade.
Standard theory says monopolies restrict output and raise prices, but possible benefits include economies of scale, R&D investment and dynamic efficiency.
Growth is shown by the curve becoming straighter.
Monopolies are illegal and always harmful.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between CPI and RPI as inflation measures?
options: A monopoly is when one country dominates world trade.
CPI and RPI always give the same inflation figure.
CPI measures consumer prices and RPI measures retail prices — that's the only difference.

Both measure price changes via a basket of goods, but RPI includes housing costs (mortgage interest) and uses an arithmetic mean; CPI excludes housing costs and uses a geometric mean — CPI is the official UK target measure.

mcqs.q: How is economic growth shown on a Production Possibility Curve?
options: Growth is shown by moving from inside the curve to a point on the curve.
By an outward shift of the entire curve — reflecting an increase in productive capacity through more or better resources, technology, or skills.
Growth is shown by the curve becoming straighter.
A monopoly is when one country dominates world trade.
